study type: Cross-sectional analysis of prospective observational data
cohort: The study analyzed data from 1774 healthy nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies from the Irish cohort of the SCOPE study, which included 68 women with preeclampsia and 171 randomly selected controls.
finding: Women with preeclampsia incurred significantly higher maternity costs, averaging EUR5243 per case, compared to EUR2452 per case for uncomplicated pregnancies, with national costs estimated between EUR6.5 and EUR9.1 million annually.
followup_time: N/A (Costs were collected through the full maternity period, including postpartum care, but no specific duration after birth is mentioned for the last observation.)
cross-section timing: Costs were aggregated over the entire maternity period (antepartum, peripartum, and postpartum care) for women recruited between November 2008 and February 2011.
